# hush_service_agent (Resource)

A service agent: an AI agent that signs in to Hush with the identity of the workload it runs on (an AWS IAM role, a Kubernetes service account, an Azure / Entra service principal or any OIDC issuer) instead of a person's sign-in. It acts as itself or, when `acts_for_users` is on, for a signed-in user. Give it apps with a `hush_mcp_application` assignment rule on `agent.id`: assigning an app to all users does not cover service agents. A client secret is managed with `hush_service_agent_client_secret`. An identity can belong to one agent at a time: to move it to another agent, remove it from the first in one apply and add it to the second in the next.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An agent running on AWS (e.g. Bedrock AgentCore) that can also act for the
# users a front end signs in for it.
resource "hush_service_agent" "summarizer" {
  name           = "summarizer"
  acts_for_users = true

  aws_iam_role {
    issuer   = "https://a1c0f603-652b-4692-937c-822f21592bdc.tokens.sts.global.api.aws"
    role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/summarizer-runtime"
  }
}

# An agent running in Kubernetes, limited to one cluster's service account.
resource "hush_service_agent" "nightly_report" {
  name = "nightly-report"

  kubernetes {
    issuer          = "https://oidc.eks.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/id/2881A7E8F2BEE882D793CDE80D900F5F"
    namespace       = "agents"
    service_account = "nightly-report"
  }
}

# An Azure AI Foundry agent, signing in with its Entra agent identity. The
# app registration (audience) must issue v2 tokens and be dedicated to Hush.
resource "hush_service_agent" "foundry_helper" {
  name = "foundry-helper"

  azure {
    tenant_id            = "8ea310af-fd38-43b1-8ff6-17df102dc19a"
    service_principal_id = "f845fb9c-55e8-4fc3-b03c-ca3fde64cdcf"
    audience             = "609677e2-6afc-4fc1-a44b-0e5e5d662b3e"
  }
}

# A front end signs users in for the summarizer with this resource.
output "summarizer_resource" {
  value = hush_service_agent.summarizer.resource
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The agent's name.

### Optional

- `acts_for_users` (Boolean) Whether the agent can act for a signed-in user, by exchanging the user's token (RFC 8693 token exchange).
- `aws_iam_role` (Block Set) An AWS IAM role, signing in with `sts:GetWebIdentityToken` tokens whose audience is the deployment's issuer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--aws_iam_role))
- `azure` (Block Set) An Azure / Entra service principal: a managed identity, an app registration or an Entra agent identity (e.g. a Foundry agent). It signs in with an app-only Entra token for `audience`, so it also sends `resource` (the gateway) when it signs in. The app registration must issue v2 tokens and be dedicated to Hush: anything that receives tokens for it could replay them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--azure))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the agent can sign in.
- `kubernetes` (Block Set) A Kubernetes service account, signing in with a projected token whose audience is the deployment's issuer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--kubernetes))
- `oidc` (Block Set) Any OIDC issuer: a token from `issuer` whose `sub` is `subject`, with the deployment's issuer as its audience. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--oidc))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `resource` (String) What a front end passes as `resource` when it signs a user in for this agent to act for them.

<a id="nestedblock--aws_iam_role"></a>
### Nested Schema for `aws_iam_role`

Required:

- `issuer` (String) The AWS account's outbound identity federation issuer, from `aws iam get-outbound-web-identity-federation-info`.
- `role_arn` (String) The role's ARN. The role needs `sts:GetWebIdentityToken`.

Optional:

- `conditions` (Block List, Max: 10) Extra checks on the token's claims; all must hold. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--aws_iam_role--conditions))

<a id="nestedblock--aws_iam_role--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `aws_iam_role.conditions`

Required:

- `claim` (List of String) The claim: its name, or a path into nested claims (up to 5 names).
- `value` (String) The value to compare with. A list claim matches if any element does.

Optional:

- `op` (String) 'eq' (equal), 'pfx' (starts with) or 'sfx' (ends with).



<a id="nestedblock--azure"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure`

Required:

- `audience` (String) The application (client) id of the app registration the identity requests tokens for, lowercase.
- `service_principal_id` (String) The service principal's object id (the token's `sub`), lowercase.
- `tenant_id` (String) The Entra tenant id, lowercase.

Optional:

- `conditions` (Block List, Max: 10) Extra checks on the token's claims; all must hold. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--azure--conditions))

<a id="nestedblock--azure--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure.conditions`

Required:

- `claim` (List of String) The claim: its name, or a path into nested claims (up to 5 names).
- `value` (String) The value to compare with. A list claim matches if any element does.

Optional:

- `op` (String) 'eq' (equal), 'pfx' (starts with) or 'sfx' (ends with).



<a id="nestedblock--kubernetes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `kubernetes`

Required:

- `issuer` (String) The cluster's OIDC issuer, as its `/.well-known/openid-configuration` reports it.
- `namespace` (String) The service account's namespace.
- `service_account` (String) The service account's name.

Optional:

- `conditions` (Block List, Max: 10) Extra checks on the token's claims; all must hold. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--kubernetes--conditions))

<a id="nestedblock--kubernetes--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `kubernetes.conditions`

Required:

- `claim` (List of String) The claim: its name, or a path into nested claims (up to 5 names).
- `value` (String) The value to compare with. A list claim matches if any element does.

Optional:

- `op` (String) 'eq' (equal), 'pfx' (starts with) or 'sfx' (ends with).



<a id="nestedblock--oidc"></a>
### Nested Schema for `oidc`

Required:

- `issuer` (String) The issuer, an https URL whose `/.well-known/openid-configuration` is public.
- `subject` (String) The token's `sub`.

Optional:

- `conditions` (Block List, Max: 10) Extra checks on the token's claims; all must hold. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--oidc--conditions))

<a id="nestedblock--oidc--conditions"></a>

- `value` (String) The value to compare with. A list claim matches if any element does.

Optional:

- `op` (String) 'eq' (equal), 'pfx' (starts with) or 'sfx' (ends with).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the agent's id. Its client secrets are separate resources.
terraform import hush_service_agent.summarizer agt-usAbCdEfGhIjKlMnOp
```
